note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management options following a recent PSA surge and repeat biopsy confirmation.

Semi-retired musician living with his partner, who prefers flexible appointment scheduling due to his self-employed status. He reports a recent increase in PSA levels, rising from 1.1 ng/mL in August 2024 to 5.8 ng/mL in January 2025, prompting this re-evaluation. He has a history of prostate cancer diagnosed earlier this year, initially managed with active surveillance. He currently experiences mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 4. He is a current smoker with a 41 pack-year history and abstains from alcohol. He has limited mobility, performing only chair-based exercises, and is currently attending physiotherapy for lower back issues. Recent appointments include thyroid screening with endocrinology and a sleep clinic evaluation for suspected obstructive sleep apnoea. He has hypercholesterolaemia but is not currently taking any active medication.

On DRE, an abnormality is palpable in the left peripheral zone at the base, consistent with clinical T stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with a BMI of 23.4 and stable vital signs including a blood pressure of 130/73 mmHg and heart rate of 80 bpm.
